_comment: PER-TEAM OPENING BOOK — canonical startup sequences. NOTHING CONSUMES THIS YET.
WHY IT EXISTS. The eval is MEASURED BLIND in the opening: Brier 0.2496-0.2559 at
turns 1-9 across four sessions, i.e. at or worse than always-guessing-50/50, and an
independent early-signal study put observables at T3 (0.1716) ahead of the engine's
own read at T9 (0.2479). So the opening is the ONE phase where overriding the search
does not fight a working component — which is the failure mode of nearly every other
lever this campaign has tried.
AND A NATURAL EXPERIMENT SAYS THE LOSS IS SEQUENCE-SHAPED. Round 3 ran a dedicated
Trick Room team (troom1: 0-Spe setters plus slow payloads, pure sequence) against a
semi-TR team that can also just attack (troom2). troom1 floored at 28.6% while troom2
TOPPED the table at 51.4% — 23pp apart, and troom2 winning rules out 'TR is simply
bad for this pilot'. The engine improvises where a human would execute a known line.
SCOPE, chosen to avoid the move-net mistake (-51pp from injecting preferences
everywhere): per-team, opening-only, condition-gated, and DEFAULT-MCTS on any failed
condition. This is not a policy over the game; it is a handful of teams whose value
IS their first few turns.
TWO STRENGTHS, both planned, neither wired yet:
weighted  each step becomes an s1 ROOT PRIOR (the advocate's proven machinery —
0.75 prior steers 20k+ visits on demand, and branch-invariance does NOT
apply to priors since they allocate exploration rather than leaf value),
so MCTS keeps its catastrophe veto.
scripted  return the order pre-search. Strictly stronger and strictly riskier.
SHIP DISCIPLINE: shadow first (log book-vs-MCTS disagreement and margins, the overlay
pattern), then a paired A/B on these teams only.
TEAM SELECTION. Ranked by how MECHANICALLY FORCED the sequence is, using
team_roles.py's resource chains and entry-gated mons — not by intuition:
snow1  Aurora Veil CANNOT be used without snow. Hard mechanical gate.
eterr1 Hawlucha's Electric Seed only fires under terrain, and consuming it is what
triggers Unburden AND powers Acrobatics. Three effects, one precondition.
ho1    screens are a 5-turn (8 with Light Clay) window the sweepers spend.

troom1 the round-3 diagnostic itself; TR is 5 turns and the payloads are 0-Spe.
  sun1   MEASURED FAILURE, added 2026-08-03: across 48 sun-team ladder games we led
         the actual sun SETTER only 8% of the time, and the three most common leads
         were Walking Wake 21%, Ceruledge 19% and Great Tusk 17% — Walking Wake
         REQUIRES sun, so we were repeatedly leading a mon that depends on a
         resource nobody had created yet. The lead is chosen by uniform
         choice_rng.choice() over the near-tie pool, so paste order carries no
         weight; the canonical-slot-1 weighting idea was never implemented, and
         this file's `lead` field is the stronger version of it.

(web2 was the fifth candidate and was REMOVED at authoring time: the validator
         found its Araquanid does not know Sticky Web, and no mon on that team does.
         See the TODO note — the whole webs sub-family is affected.)
SCHEMA
lead        species to send at team preview (step 0 — this also kills the
preview-maximin / T1-repudiation split at its source: one plan instead
of maximin-then-override)
steps       ordered; the FIRST step whose `when` holds and whose `do` is legal is
the book's suggestion. No match = MCTS, unchanged.
when        ALL keys must hold. Vocabulary is deliberately tiny and every key is
checkable against a poke-env Battle:
active        our active species (normalized id)
max_turn      battle.turn <= n
field_up      one of: snow/sun/rain/sand/electricterrain/
grassyterrain/psychicterrain/trickroom/screens
field_down    same vocabulary, negated
hp_at_least   our active's hp fraction >= x
unused        this move has not yet been used by us this battle
do          move id, or 'switch <species>'
why         human-facing rationale. Never parsed.
REVIEW RULE: every `do` must be a move the team actually carries (or a switch to a
mon it actually has) — a step naming a move nobody has is a silent no-op, which is
the quietest possible way for this file to be useless. tests/test_opening_book.py
cross-checks every step against the paste.
OCTOBER CAVEAT: scripts are scoutable. Fine against non-adapting bots; revisit
before qualifying.

steps.why: Snow Warning sets snow on entry, and Aurora Veil is ILLEGAL without it — so this is the one turn the whole team is built around. Light Clay makes it 8 turns; every later step spends them.
veil is up and its job is done; Encore locks the opponent's answer so the payload gets a free entry rather than a predicted one.
Belly Drum FAILS at or below 50% HP and costs half, so it must happen at full HP behind the veil — the veil is what makes surviving the drop survivable.
Electric Surge already set the terrain on entry, so turn 1 is free for the hazard this team otherwise has no setter for.
Pincurchin's job is done once terrain and Spikes are up; Memento halves the opponent's attack AND hands Hawlucha the free entry its Seed plan needs.
the Seed has already been consumed on entry, so Unburden has doubled Speed and Acrobatics is item-less and doubled — this is the turn the sweep is set up, not the turn it starts.
Prankster gives it +1 priority, so it lands before the opponent acts. Physical first: the sweepers behind it are frailer physically.
the second half of the window. Light Clay makes both 8 turns, which is the entire resource this team plays for.
screens are up and Grimmsnarl has nothing left to add; Parting Shot drops both attacking stats AND pivots a sweeper in for free — the safest possible entry.
the round-3 diagnostic that greenlit this file: troom1 floored at 28.6% while semi-TR troom2 topped the table, so the engine is not finding this line on its own.
Cresselia is the backup setter; Mental Herb protects the attempt from Taunt exactly once.
under the room Ursaluna moves FIRST, and Guts Facade is why the team accepted a 0-Spe payload at all. The room is 5 turns; spend them attacking.

Drought already set the sun ON ENTRY, so no turn is spent creating the resource — turn 1 is free for the hazard. This is why leading the setter costs nothing here and gains everything: the sun clock starts at turn 1 instead of whenever it happens to come in.
Torkoal's other job. Removing hazards protects the Life Orb Venusaur that has to switch in repeatedly, and it is doing this while the sun clock it started keeps running.

under sun Growth raises BOTH attacking stats by two stages instead of one, and Chlorophyll has already doubled Venusaur's Speed — so this single turn is worth two boosts and a speed tier. Outside sun it is worth neither, which is the whole argument for leading Torkoal.

Psychic Surge sets the terrain ON ENTRY, so turn 1 costs nothing and is free for the second resource. Terrain Extender makes it 8 turns against Trick Room's 5, so the priority block OUTLASTS the room and covers a second setup — which is the whole reason this pairing exists: Trick Room inverts speed, and priority is the one thing that ignores the inversion.
the room is running and Indeedee has nothing left to add; Encore locks the opponent's answer so a 0-Spe payload gets a free entry rather than a predicted one.
under the room Ursaluna moves FIRST, and Guts Facade is why a 0-Spe payload was acceptable. Psychic Terrain is what stops it being revenge-killed by priority, which is how slow sweepers normally die.
